---
title: "Research"
---

My research sits at the intersection of **causal inference**, **biostatistics**, and **computational epidemiology**, with a focus on methods that stay valid when randomisation is impossible and the data are observational.

## Causal estimation with complex exposures

Multicausal and multivalued treatment effects in the potential outcomes framework: what to do when a treatment has more than two levels, the nuisance models are learned by machine learning, and the estimand must remain interpretable. Double-robust estimation, cross-fitting, and influence-function-based inference. See [Software](../software.qmd) for the `tmleMulti` implementation.

## Targeted learning & semiparametric efficiency

Targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE), doubly robust learning, and the semiparametric efficiency theory that makes these estimators valid and publishable. A central thread of my work is the *influence function* and *delta method* as unifying tools for variance estimation in medical statistics.

## Conformal inference for causal questions

Distribution-free uncertainty quantification with finite-sample coverage guarantees. Together with my PhD students we develop conformal methods for causal estimands, where the outcome model is learned by machine learning or the sample is small.

## Computational epidemiology & inequalities in cancer

Applied causal questions in population health: socioeconomic inequalities in cancer outcomes, the effect of emergency presentation on cancer survival, and reproducible, data-adaptive estimators for cancer epidemiology.

## Open problems

I welcome collaborations and prospective students on: multicausal treatment effects with machine-learned nuisance models, conformal inference for causal estimands, and reproducible computational tutorials that bridge the gap between methodological advances and applied researchers.
